title: The spending is public. The source isn’t. — animated money trail
description: Looping animation of the dark-money trail: Step 1 (PAC spent $10.7M opposing a candidate — filed) and Step 2 (a nonprofit gave that PAC $3,000,000 — named in the PAC’s ledger) appear with green checks; the arrow then drops into a black Step 3 void with a pulsing “?” — “Who gave the nonprofit the $3M? No filing exists — none is required.”
alt_text: Animation titled “The spending is public. The source isn’t.” Two green-outlined boxes appear with checkmarks: a super PAC spent $10.7 million opposing a candidate, every receipt on record; a nonprofit gave that PAC $3,000,000, named in the PAC’s ledger. An arrow leads to a black box with a pulsing question mark: who gave the nonprofit the $3 million — no filing exists, none is required.
creator: Daniel Ismael Aguilar
usage_note: Data visualization compiled from public FEC filings and cited press reporting. Figures: $11,077,173 spent opposing Graham Platner vs. $323,426 supporting (FEC Schedule E, deduplicated, Oct 2025 – Jul 8, 2026).
accessibility_note: First frame shows only the title; pair with section-hidden-money-1600x900.png where a meaningful preview frame is required.
